references.text: John 13:21 describes the same moment where Jesus is troubled in spirit and reveals that one of the disciples will betray him, confirming that the devil had already laid plans in Judas' heart.
In John 13:27 the action from verse 2 is completed; after Jesus gives Judas a piece of bread, the devil enters him, and he leaves the table to carry out the betrayal.

Matthew 26:14-16 provides the historical context for Judas' actions, where he goes to the chief priests and agrees to betray Jesus for money, which is the concrete execution of what was laid in his heart.
Luke 22:3-4 confirms that it was Satan who entered Judas before he went to the chief priests to negotiate the betrayal, a direct parallel to the description in John 13:2.
John 17:12 refers back to Judas as 'the one doomed to destruction' and identifies him as the one who was betrayed, confirming that he was the one the devil used to hand over Jesus.
